items.title: Screenshots as code: shipping Play Store assets from a unit test
items.summary: Updating Play Store screenshots usually goes like this: someone takes captures on a device, a designer puts them into frames, someone else translates the headlines, and the whole thing goes out of date at the next redesign. At Aircall we replaced that process with a JVM unit test.This talk covers a small tool module that renders our real Compose screens from the same fixtures as their Android Studio previews. It runs headlessly with Robolectric and Roborazzi, so there’s no emulator, no device and no golden images. Each screen goes into a real Pixel device frame on a mesh gradient background with a localized headline, and the output is Play-compliant PNGs for every screen and locale. A manual CI job then uploads them through the Play Developer API as a single atomic edit.You’ll leave with a pattern you can reuse to treat store assets like any other build output: reviewable, reproducible and one click away from the store.
